title: Arrays & lists
examples: How do I access the third item in the list?
What is the difference between a list and an array?
Can you show me how to loop through a 2D array?

explain.say: Today we are learning about arrays and lists in programming.

items: Arrays store multiple values in order.
Lists are a common way to implement arrays.
They allow grouping related data together.

explain.say: First we need to understand indexing which is how we find items.
Next we look at two dimensional arrays which are like tables.
Traversal means visiting every single item in the array one by one.

items: End when all items are processed

explain.say: In real life you use arrays when tracking student scores.
A common mistake is thinking indexing starts at one.

faq.q: Why do we start counting from zero when indexing?
faq.a: In most programming languages, counting starts at zero because of how computer memory is structured. This is a fundamental rule of the system.
asks: Why is the first index zero?

faq.q: What is the difference between a list and an array?
faq.a: For many purposes, they are the same, but sometimes a list allows for more flexible resizing than a traditional array.
asks: Which one is better to use?

faq.q: How do I find the total sum of all numbers in an array?
faq.a: You must use a loop to visit every element and add its value to a running total variable.
asks: Can I sum an array without a loop?
What function calculates the total sum?

faq.q: What is a two dimensional array used for?
faq.a: They are perfect for representing grids, like a chessboard or a spreadsheet of data points.
asks: What does a row and column mean together?

faq.q: What is 'traversal' in the context of data structures?
faq.a: Traversal simply means going through every single item in the collection in a specific, orderly sequence.
asks: Do I have to visit every item?
What is the process of going through a list?

facts: Arrays store a fixed sequence of elements of the same type.
Indexing allows programmers to access elements by their position number.
A two dimensional array requires two indices: one for the row and one for the column.
Traversal involves iterating through every element from start to finish.

quiz.say: If an array has five items, what is the index of the very last item?
quiz.show: Index of last item in 5-item array?
quiz.why: Because indexing starts at zero, the fifth item will be at index four.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because zero is the index of the first item, not the last.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it only accounts for the second item in the sequence.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake because people naturally count starting from one.

quiz.say: To access the data in the second row and third column of a grid, what indices would you use?
quiz.why: The first index selects the row, and the second index selects the column, both starting at zero.

wrong.0: This is incorrect as it does not correctly map the second row and third column.
wrong.2: This assumes the count starts at one for both rows and columns.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it uses the wrong index for the column position.

quiz.say: Which process describes visiting every single element in a collection?
quiz.why: Traversal is the specific term used in computer science for systematically visiting every item.

wrong.0: Storing is the action of putting data into the array, not reading it out.
wrong.2: Indexing is only about finding the position of one specific item.
wrong.3: Declaring is the act of setting up the variable or structure itself.
